pr_title: Support index sorting with nested fields
pr_body:
This PR piggy-backs on recent changes in Lucene 9.11.1 (https://github.com/apache/lucene/pull/12829, https://github.com/apache/lucene/pull/13341/), setting the parent doc when nested fields are present. This allows moving nested documents along with parent ones during sorting.

With this change, sorting is now allowed on fields outside nested objects. Sorting on fields within nested objects is still not supported (throws an exception).

Fixes #107349
pr_comments: Hi @kkrik-es, I've created a changelog YAML for you.
This seems important enough, added a highlight note.

issue_context.title: Index sorting and nested fields
issue_context.body:
### Description

In Elasticsearch index sorting does not work if nested fields are used. This Elasticsearch limitation derives from a Lucene limitation [which has been fixed recently](https://github.com/apache/lucene/pull/12829). We currently use index sorting for time series indices but plan to use it for logs too.

Note that at the moment nested fields are also not supported in synthetic source but we plan to address this limitation in #106460.

The limitation behind using index sorting and nested fields is a result of the fact that nested documents need to be written contiguously to their parent document inside the Lucene segment to make sure that the parent/child relationship is correctly mantained. Index sorting used to break this relationship in Lucene ,since sorting of parent documents was missing the logic to move nested document next to the linked parent document. This has been fixed recently so we need to make sure we make use of the Lucene functionality so that we can remove the limitation in Elasticsearch too. Failing to support nested fields while index sorting is used might make using the new "logs" index mode not possible, since `nested` fields are used by a few integrations indexing logs in logs-\*-\* data streams.

After reading the description of the Lucene fix it looks like the parent child relationship in Lucene is accomplished by using a (common) numeric value which is stored using numeric doc values. As a result, taking advantage of this feature in Lucene might require we change our implementation of nested fields to use numeric doc values too.
comments:
>  As a result, taking advantage of this feature in Lucene might require we change our implementation of nested fields to use numeric doc values too.

FWIW I would not change the way that we implement nested fields. I would just configure a new special parent field via `IndexWriterConfig#setParentField`, and still index/search nested fields the way we have always indexed them. This would result in a bit of duplication as there would be 2 ways of identifying root documents, but I would not consider this a blocker.

review_comments: I wonder how this works when the nested field is added as an update to the mapping? Should we always set the parent field in case a nested field is added later?
Good point, I was thinking about this but wasn't sure of the implications. @jpountz any thoughts on this?
I asked a similar question to @s1monw a while back, and he suggested always adding the parent field when an index sort is configured.
Excellent, this simplifies things. Lemme update the PR.
Maybe include the reason why parent field is always enabled in the comment too?
Right, this was added in the last iteration.

I wonder if we need to keep this limitation for existing index? This would mean checking the index version to ensure that this mode is not activated on indices with an index sort and already indexed documents.
I see, the problem is that existing indexes do not have the parent field set and a mapping update may introduce a nested object. That's correct, we need to check for the version here.
